title: finding(docs/guide): schema-rendering.md's Data Context teaches a `data` prop the evaluator never reads, and a bare `${user.name}` spelling no scope holds — three passages, measured 4 legs
body:
Measured while implementing #7680 — the `chart` node on the same page, whose dispatched
surface is that node alone. This is a different key family on the same guide, so it is filed
here rather than repaired on that card.

Measured on `origin/main` `4922b83`.

⚠️ JSX tag shapes are spelled out in words below: a tag-shaped fragment does not survive this
field, and the passages this card is about are exactly JSX elements.

## The site — three passages, one mechanism

`content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`:

- `:75` **Data Context** — states that `SchemaRenderer` accepts a `data` prop that provides
  context for expressions, and shows a `SchemaRenderer` element carrying `schema={schema}`
  and `data={data}`, with no provider anywhere.
- `:89` **Accessing Data in Schemas** — teaches the expression spelling
  `"content": "Welcome, ${user.name}!"` against that `data`.
- `:365` **Best Practice 2** — repeats the same element, same prop.

The `:70` example (`"content": "Total Users: ${stats.totalUsers}"`) uses the same bare
spelling.

## Both coordinates are wrong, measured through a real render

`SchemaRendererProps` declares exactly one prop, `schema`
(`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:500`); every other prop is forwarded to whichever
component the schema names. The expression context is built at `SchemaRenderer.tsx:645` out of
`usePredicateScope()` plus `data: dataSource`, `current_user` and `page` — and `dataSource`
comes from `SchemaRendererProvider`. So the `data` prop reaches the evaluator through nothing,
and a bare `${user.name}` is looked up in a scope that holds `data` / `page` / `current_user`,
never `user`.

Four legs, one `text` node each, real `SchemaRenderer`, reading `container.textContent`:

| leg | wiring | expression | rendered |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `data` prop, no provider (**what the page teaches**) | `${user.name}` | `Welcome, ${user.name}!` |
| B | `data` prop, no provider | `${data.user.name}` | `Welcome, !` |
| C | provider `dataSource` | `${data.user.name}` | `Welcome, John!` |
| D | provider `dataSource` | `${user.name}` | `Welcome, ${user.name}!` |

Leg A is the page's own snippet pair, and it puts the raw source on screen. Leg C is the only
green one, and it differs from the page in **both** coordinates. B and D are the controls that
keep the two halves apart: B shows the prop supplies nothing even with the right prefix, D
shows the prefix is needed even with the right wiring. So this is one page teaching two
independent errors, not one error with two spellings.

The failure is silent in the way this page's family always is: nothing throws, nothing warns,
the characters the author typed are what the reader sees.

## Why this is not #7680

#7680 is node-level `data` on a `chart` — rows, not expression context; it is refused by
`ChartSchema` and dropped by `ChartRenderer`. This card is the guide's evaluator wiring, it
spans three passages, and it is equally wrong for every node type on the page.

## What a repair would decide

Whether the page should teach `SchemaRendererProvider` with `dataSource` and the `data.`
prefix (the wiring every measured-green example in this repo uses), or whether
`SchemaRenderer` should grow a real `data` prop that seeds the evaluator. The first is a docs
change; the second is a renderer contract change and a maintainer decision. Worth one look at
whether the sibling guides teach the same prop.

⛔ Deliberately unassigned and unlabelled, for triage.
